BUILDPLAN.md T-18 (M3).

Review surface (local, served by the CLI): one screen per candidate, accept/reject-with-reason/edit-and-reverify, difficulty judged, **affirm** as a blocking gate with who/when, middle-beat and quoted-output checks; §11.1 trope matches highlighted beside `explains`, `why_tempting` and `hint` as warnings that block nothing (`SPEC.md` §7.4, D-23)

Criteria: AC-19–22, AC-72–74, AC-88, AC-95, G-12
Harness hooks: see EVALUATION.md rows for those IDs; `just test` is the inner loop (≤ 60 s).
Depends on (BUILDPLAN): T-14, T-15b
BUILDPLAN notes: —

Orchestrator notes: Reads `near_duplicate_of` written by T-17.

Workflow mode: inline-full. Terminal pre-merge status: review. PR base: origin/main.
Standing clauses: criteria outrank SPEC on behaviour, state, payloads and copy; SPEC outranks the prototype, which wins on visual detail only. Never write down what a program prints. Answer position is a uniform draw from the date, never balanced. Miri proves absence of UB on executed paths only. Colour is never the only signal. Code never causes horizontal page scroll. Never `git add -A`. Signing goes through 1Password: retry once, then escalate.

Plan: filled in by the delegator's plan phase.

RULING (client, 2026-10-11: '1, narrow it into the TUI'). PQ-23 is narrowed, not cancelled. PR #64 (draft, codex/organizer-trace-preview, head 50cd985, prototypes/organizer-tui) already gives the organizer TUI: preview, the trace step navigator, explicit reveal, and scheduling through the Python scheduler. That replaces this ticket's preview screens and its 'local web surface served by the CLI' form. PR #64 says review decisions are not implemented and that preview and scheduling leave bank records unchanged, so this ticket keeps exactly that part.

NEW SCOPE, as screens in the organizer TUI: accept; reject with a reason; edit and re-verify (the verifier writes verified output, never the TUI, AC-7); difficulty judged; AFFIRM as a blocking gate that records who and when; middle-beat and quoted-output checks; SPEC 11.1 trope matches shown beside explains, why_tempting and hint as warnings that block nothing (D-23). Criteria unchanged: AC-19-22, AC-72-74, AC-88, AC-95, G-12. Carried: GAP-24 (bind the affirmation to the text it affirmed: explains, why_tempting, trace; an edit sets review.status 'edited' and clears it), the F-52 ruling (q3's hand affirmation is an existing record to display and keep, never rewritten; q4/q7/q8 get traces and an affirmation through this ticket; q8 also waits on F-15), and the near_duplicate_of display from T-17.

GATE: held until PR #64 merges; then base on origin/main and plan against the merged TUI's crate layout. Writes to bank records go through the pipeline's existing bank and verify code (no second writer in Rust unless the plan argues for it and the Orchestrator rules). If PR #64 does not merge, this ticket returns to the client before any dispatch.

REVIEW PQ-23 (orchestrator, exact head) — PR #80 at b64b723, base 4673e12 (12 commits, 28 files, +4008/−91)
Verdict: PASS-WITH-NITS. Nothing blocks the merge.

CI at b64b723: run 38310132334, `just test` and `just test-full` both SUCCESS. The harness burst test passed in CI as well, which supports the client's "unrelated" call on the local failure. PR is MERGEABLE/CLEAN.

What holds (two Sonnet passes plus orchestrator spot checks):
- The q3 RULING is implemented. bank.affirmation_state returns "unbound" when there is no digest, and is_affirmed accepts only "bound". audit.in_reserve and schedule.refusal both go through it. No affirmation path reads verified.legacy. bank-audit shows nyc reserve 0.
- affirm requires an accepted or edited status and an explicit name (--by or POPQUIZ_ORGANIZER; an empty --by does not fall back). AC-73 wrong-quote blockers gate both accept and affirm. Every edit and every reject clears affirmed_by, affirmed_at and affirmed_digest. The digest covers source, options plus why_tempting, hint, explains (legacy included) and the trace stdout row.
- b64b723 is correct: a rejected question stays rejected on edit, and an unreviewed one stays unreviewed.
- No writes to bank/questions or verified files. The diff is empty under bank/questions/, room/, docs/adr and verify.py. Tests and the recording driver use temp copies of the fixtures, and an autouse fixture hashes real bank/ before and after. The TUI writes no file and drives everything through `python -m popquiz.review`. --by is passed only when POPQUIZ_ORGANIZER is set, with env_remove. Flag-like values use --x=value. There is no literal identity in the TUI source.
- Verification wording is honest: "Miri evidence covers executed paths only", and the digest "does not authenticate who wrote it".
- The PR body names the RULING, the deviations, and the burst failure as unrelated.

Nits (follow-up ticket, not blocking):
1. bank/schema/question.schema.json:237: the affirmed_digest description still says an absent digest "is read as legacy". That contradicts the RULING; it should say "is unbound and counts nowhere".
2. prototypes/organizer-tui/recordings/review-gate.cast:1: the header embeds a local scratchpad path containing the macOS username (public repo). Strip it.
3. Tests: rejected-stays-rejected is covered only on the no-program-change edit path. Add the re-verify path (_verify_into_bank) and the unreviewed case. An identical-content edit of an affirmed question is untested.
4. review.py: quotes_checked survives edits while the span text survives. That is probably intended (AC-73 keys on the span) but undocumented.
5. review.rs:235: the id is passed positionally with no `--` (real ids are q<N>). review.rs:321: `changed` is set on "Not recorded" (harmless reload).
Already deferred by the delegator: multi-blocker sentences, newline in --by, predictable editor temp path, panic-unsafe env cleanup, absolute git-status guard, Esc can't cancel re-verify.
